title: App caches
why: Data apps downloaded or worked out earlier, kept to open things faster. Apps rebuild it when needed, so removing it is safe.

title: macOS caches
why: Caches made by macOS and Apple apps. They are rebuilt too, but some hold sign-in or sync state, so take a look first.

title: Command-line tool caches
why: Caches that command-line tools keep in ~/.cache. Tools download or rebuild them, but check for anything you still need.

title: Chrome cache
why: Web pages and images Chrome saved to load sites faster. Chrome fetches them again as you browse.

title: Chrome graphics cache
why: Compiled graphics shaders Chrome keeps to draw pages faster. Chrome compiles them again.

title: Chrome GPU cache
why: Per-profile graphics caches in Chrome. Chrome rebuilds them; your history and passwords are not here.

title: Chrome application cache
why: Old offline web-app storage from Chrome. Sites download it again when needed.

title: Chromium graphics caches
why: Graphics caches from Chromium. It rebuilds them the next time it draws a page.

title: Firefox cache
why: Web pages and images Firefox saved to load sites faster. Firefox fetches them again.

title: Arc cache
why: Web pages and images Arc saved to load sites faster. Arc fetches them again as you browse.

title: Brave cache
why: Web pages and images Brave saved to load sites faster. Brave fetches them again.

title: Edge cache
why: Web pages and images Microsoft Edge saved to load sites faster. Edge fetches them again.

title: Opera cache
why: Web pages and images Opera saved to load sites faster. Opera fetches them again.

title: Vivaldi cache
why: Web pages and images Vivaldi saved to load sites faster. Vivaldi fetches them again.

title: Zen browser cache
why: Web pages and images the Zen browser saved to load sites faster. It fetches them again.

title: Slack cache
why: Images, files and compiled code Slack keeps to start faster. Slack downloads or rebuilds them.

title: Discord cache
why: Images, files and compiled code Discord keeps to start faster. Discord downloads or rebuilds them.

title: Notion cache
why: Images, files and compiled code Notion keeps to start faster. Notion downloads or rebuilds them.

title: Figma cache
why: Images, files and compiled code Figma keeps to start faster. Figma downloads or rebuilds them.

title: WhatsApp cache
why: Images, files and compiled code WhatsApp keeps to start faster. WhatsApp downloads or rebuilds them.

title: Signal cache
why: Images, files and compiled code Signal keeps to start faster. Signal downloads or rebuilds them.

title: Linear cache
why: Images, files and compiled code Linear keeps to start faster. Linear downloads or rebuilds them.

title: Postman cache
why: Images, files and compiled code Postman keeps to start faster. Postman downloads or rebuilds them.

title: Microsoft Teams cache
why: Images and compiled code classic Teams keeps to start faster. Teams downloads them again.

title: Obsidian cache
why: Compiled code and graphics caches from the Obsidian app. Your notes live elsewhere and are not touched.

title: Zoom cache
why: Temporary files Zoom keeps between meetings. Zoom makes new ones next time.

title: Spotify offline music
why: Spotify keeps your downloaded songs and podcasts here. Removing it would delete your downloads.

title: Apple Music downloads
why: Music and Podcasts keep streamed and offline audio here. Removing it can delete downloads, so Dustpan leaves it.

title: iCloud sync cache
why: iCloud keeps sync state here. Removing it can force a full re-sync, so Dustpan leaves it alone.

title: LM Studio models
why: Models you downloaded in LM Studio. They are large to fetch again, so Dustpan never lists them.

title: Ollama models
why: Models you pulled with Ollama. Remove one with ollama rm in Terminal when you are done with it.

title: Hugging Face sign-in
why: Your Hugging Face access tokens, kept beside its cache. Removing them signs you out, so Dustpan never lists them.

title: Steam caches
why: Store pages, shader and download caches from Steam. Your games stay installed; Steam rebuilds these.

title: EA app caches
why: Browser and overlay caches from the EA app. It downloads them again; your games are not touched.

title: Minecraft launcher cache
why: Web pages the Minecraft launcher saved. Your worlds and saves live elsewhere and stay put.

title: Lunar Client caches
why: Download caches from Lunar Client. It fetches them again when you start a game.

title: Adobe media cache
why: Preview and audio files Adobe video apps make while you edit. They are rebuilt when you open a project.

title: Dropbox cache
why: Old file versions Dropbox keeps while syncing. Dropbox clears them over time; your files are not here.

title: Google Drive file cache
why: Local copies of files from Google Drive. Drive downloads them again; offline files will need a network.

title: Microsoft AutoUpdate cache
why: Files Microsoft AutoUpdate downloaded while checking for updates. It downloads new ones when needed.

title: Google updater cache
why: Files Google's updater keeps while updating Chrome and other Google apps. It downloads new ones when needed.

title: Crash-reporter caches
why: Crash reports apps saved to send to their makers. They have been sent already or are out of date.

title: Map tiles cache
why: Map tiles macOS saved for Maps and location features. They download again when you look at a map.

title: App logs
why: Records apps write about what they did. Useful only when tracking down a problem; apps start new ones.

title: Crash reports
why: Reports macOS wrote when an app crashed or hung. Only needed if you plan to send one to a developer.

title: Simulator logs
why: Logs from iOS simulators. The simulator writes new ones each time it runs.

title: JetBrains IDE logs
why: Logs from IntelliJ, PyCharm and other JetBrains IDEs. They start new ones on the next launch.

title: Homebrew logs
why: Build logs Homebrew kept from installing packages. Only useful if an install failed.

title: Microsoft Teams logs
why: Diagnostic logs from classic Microsoft Teams. Teams writes new ones as it runs.

title: Minecraft logs
why: Game logs and crash reports from Minecraft. Your worlds are not stored here.

title: Minecraft launcher logs
why: Log files the Minecraft launcher writes on each start. New ones appear next time.

title: Lunar Client logs
why: Logs from Lunar Client. It writes new ones each time you play.

title: Steam logs
why: Logs from Steam. Only useful when tracking down a Steam problem.

title: EA app logs
why: Logs from the EA app. It writes new ones as it runs.

title: Obsidian logs
why: Log files from the Obsidian app. Your notes are not touched.

title: Cacher and Kite logs
why: Logs from the Cacher and Kite tools. They write new ones when they run.

title: wget log
why: Log file wget leaves in your home folder when run in the background.

title: npm logs
why: Debug logs npm writes after each command. Only useful right after a failed install.

title: Gradle daemon logs
why: Logs and state from old Gradle background processes. Gradle starts fresh ones.

title: Docker Desktop logs
why: Logs from Docker Desktop. Docker writes new ones as it runs.

title: OrbStack logs
why: Logs from OrbStack. It writes new ones as it runs.

title: VS Code logs
why: Session logs from VS Code. It writes new ones every time it starts.

title: Claude app logs
why: Logs from the Claude desktop app. It writes new ones as it runs.

title: Saved window state
why: Where apps remember open windows to restore them at launch. Removing it just opens apps with fresh windows.

title: Unsaved documents
why: Copies of documents you haven't saved yet. Dustpan never touches them.

title: Disk images in Downloads
why: Disk images you downloaded to install apps. Once the app is in Applications, the image is no longer needed.

title: Installer packages in Downloads
why: Installer packages you already ran. The app stays installed without them.

title: Zip files in Downloads
why: Zip archives, often apps you already unpacked. Check none hold files you still need.

title: Xcode archives in Downloads
why: Xcode download archives (.xip). Once Xcode is installed, the archive is no longer needed.

title: Installers on the Desktop
why: Disk images and installer packages on your Desktop. Once installed, the app doesn't need them.

title: iPhone and iPad updates
why: Old system updates downloaded for an iPhone or iPad. Finder downloads a fresh one when needed.

title: App update downloads
why: Updates apps downloaded through their built-in updater. Apps download again if an update is still due.

title: Electron app update downloads
why: Update files left by apps like Slack or VS Code after updating. The update is already installed.

title: Unfinished Steam downloads
why: Game downloads Steam has not finished. Steam restarts them if you still want the game.

title: Homebrew downloads
why: Packages Homebrew downloaded before installing. Already installed; brew downloads them again if needed.

title: Microsoft update downloads
why: Office updates Microsoft AutoUpdate already installed. It downloads new ones when needed.

title: Trash
why: Files you already moved to the Trash. Emptied only with Empty Trash, after you confirm the size.

title: Xcode DerivedData
why: Build products and indexes for your Xcode projects. Xcode rebuilds them the next time you build.

title: Xcode archives
why: App builds you archived for release, with their debug symbols. Keep the ones you may need for crash reports.

title: iOS device support
why: Debug files Xcode copied from an iPhone or iPad. Xcode copies them again when you connect that device.

title: watchOS device support
why: Debug files Xcode copied from an Apple Watch. Xcode copies them again when you connect that device.

title: tvOS device support
why: Debug files Xcode copied from an Apple TV. Xcode copies them again when you connect that device.

title: visionOS device support
why: Debug files Xcode copied from a Vision Pro. Xcode copies them again when you connect that device.

title: macOS device support
why: Debug files Xcode copied from a Mac. Xcode copies them again when you connect that device.

title: iOS device logs
why: Logs Xcode pulled from connected devices. Xcode pulls new ones when it needs them.

title: Xcode products
why: Builds Xcode kept for distribution and testing. Keep any you still need to share.

title: SwiftUI preview builds
why: Builds Xcode makes for SwiftUI previews. Xcode makes them again when you open a preview.

title: Xcode documentation cache
why: Downloaded documentation Xcode keeps for quick lookups. Xcode downloads it again when needed.

title: Xcode cache
why: Download and index caches Xcode keeps. Xcode rebuilds them as you work.

title: Simulator caches
why: Caches the iOS Simulator builds for faster launches. It rebuilds them when it starts.

title: Caches inside simulators
why: Caches that apps inside your simulators made. They rebuild them the next time they run.

title: Simulator temporary files
why: Temporary files left inside simulators. Apps make new ones as they run.

title: Test simulators
why: Simulator clones Xcode made for parallel testing. Xcode makes new ones when you run tests.

title: Playground simulators
why: Simulators Xcode made to run playgrounds. Xcode makes them again when you run a playground.

title: Instruments caches
why: Symbol caches Instruments keeps. It rebuilds them the next time you profile.

title: npm cache
why: Every package npm downloaded, kept to install faster. npm downloads them again when needed.

title: npx packages
why: Packages npx fetched to run one-off commands. npx fetches them again next time.

title: npm prebuilt binaries
why: Prebuilt native modules npm downloaded. npm downloads them again when needed.

title: Yarn cache
why: Packages Yarn downloaded, kept to install faster. Yarn downloads them again when needed.

title: pnpm store
why: Packages pnpm downloaded once and linked into projects. Installed projects keep working; pnpm refetches the rest.

title: Bun cache
why: Packages Bun downloaded, kept to install faster. Bun downloads them again when needed.

title: Deno cache
why: Modules Deno downloaded and compiled. Deno fetches them again when a script needs them.

title: node-gyp headers
why: Node.js headers downloaded to build native modules. They download again when needed.

title: Electron downloads
why: Electron runtimes downloaded for building apps. They download again on the next build.

title: Cypress binaries
why: Test-runner apps Cypress downloaded. Cypress downloads the right version again when you install it.

title: Puppeteer browsers
why: Browsers Puppeteer downloaded for testing. Reinstall with npm when you need them.

title: TypeScript cache
why: Type definitions downloaded for editors. Editors download them again when needed.

title: Prisma engines
why: Database engine binaries Prisma downloaded. Prisma downloads them again on the next generate.

title: pip cache
why: Python packages pip downloaded, kept to install faster. pip downloads them again when needed.

title: Pipenv cache
why: Python packages Pipenv downloaded. Pipenv downloads them again when needed.

title: Poetry caches
why: Python packages Poetry downloaded. Poetry downloads them again when needed.

title: Poetry virtual environments
why: Python environments Poetry made for your projects. Run poetry install to make them again.

title: Conda package cache
why: Package archives conda downloaded. Environments keep working; conda downloads them again if needed.

title: pre-commit environments
why: Hook environments pre-commit set up. It sets them up again on the next commit.

title: Homebrew metadata
why: Package lists and boot caches Homebrew keeps. Homebrew downloads them again on the next update.

title: CocoaPods cache
why: Pods CocoaPods downloaded. pod install downloads them again when needed.

title: Carthage cache
why: Frameworks Carthage downloaded and built. Carthage fetches them again on the next update.

title: Swift Package Manager cache
why: Swift packages downloaded for your projects. Xcode and swift build fetch them again.

title: Cargo registry cache
why: Rust crates Cargo downloaded and unpacked. Cargo downloads them again on the next build.

title: Cargo git checkouts
why: Git dependencies Cargo checked out. Cargo checks them out again on the next build.

title: rustup downloads
why: Leftover downloads from installing Rust toolchains. Your installed toolchains are not here.

title: Go build cache
why: Compiled Go packages kept to build faster. Go rebuilds them on the next build.

title: Go module cache
why: Go modules downloaded for your projects. Go fetches them again when you build; that needs a network.

title: Gradle caches
why: Libraries and build outputs Gradle downloaded. Gradle downloads them again on the next build.

title: Gradle distributions
why: Gradle versions the wrapper downloaded. Projects download the version they need again.

title: Maven repository
why: Java libraries Maven downloaded. Maven fetches them again, but locally installed builds would need rebuilding.

title: Android build cache
why: Caches the Android tools keep. They rebuild them on the next build.

title: Android Studio caches
why: Indexes and caches Android Studio keeps. It rebuilds them when you open a project.

title: JetBrains IDE caches
why: Indexes and caches IntelliJ, PyCharm and other JetBrains IDEs keep. They rebuild them on the next launch.

title: Composer cache
why: PHP packages Composer downloaded. Composer downloads them again when needed.

title: Bundler cache
why: Ruby gems Bundler downloaded. Bundler downloads them again when needed.

title: NuGet packages
why: .NET packages NuGet downloaded. dotnet restore downloads them again.

title: Conan packages
why: C and C++ packages Conan downloaded or built. Conan fetches or builds them again when needed.

title: Dart and Flutter packages
why: Packages Dart and Flutter downloaded. flutter pub get downloads them again.

title: Cabal packages
why: Haskell packages Cabal downloaded. Cabal downloads them again when needed.

title: Terraform plugin cache
why: Providers Terraform downloaded. terraform init downloads them again.

title: ccache
why: Compiler outputs ccache keeps to rebuild C and C++ faster. Builds still work, just slower the first time.

title: sccache
why: Compiler outputs sccache keeps to rebuild faster. Builds still work, just slower the first time.

title: golangci-lint cache
why: Lint results kept to check Go code faster. golangci-lint works them out again on the next run.

title: Docker disk image
why: Docker's virtual disk with your images and containers. Free space with docker system prune inside Docker instead.

title: Docker Desktop caches
why: Temporary files Docker Desktop keeps. Docker makes new ones as it runs.

title: Docker CLI caches
why: Build caches from the Docker command-line tools. Clear them with docker buildx prune inside Docker instead.

title: Vagrant boxes
why: Base images Vagrant downloaded. Remove ones you no longer use with vagrant box remove.

title: Unity cache
why: Downloaded packages and assets Unity keeps. Unity downloads them again when a project needs them.

title: Java heap dumps
why: Memory snapshots Java apps saved after a crash. Only useful while debugging that crash.

title: OrbStack cache
why: Caches OrbStack keeps. Your containers and machines are not stored here.

title: Cursor caches
why: Web and graphics caches the Cursor editor keeps. Cursor rebuilds them; your code is not touched.

title: Cursor CachedData
why: Compiled code from earlier Cursor versions. Cursor makes new copies when it starts.

title: Cursor extension downloads
why: Extension installers Cursor downloaded. Installed extensions keep working.

title: Cursor logs
why: Session logs from Cursor. It writes new ones each time it starts.

title: Cursor app cache
why: Update and compile caches for Cursor. Cursor makes them again.

title: VS Code CachedData
why: Compiled code from earlier VS Code versions. VS Code makes new copies when it starts.

title: VS Code extension downloads
why: Extension installers VS Code downloaded. Installed extensions keep working.

title: VS Code caches
why: Web and graphics caches VS Code keeps. VS Code rebuilds them; your code is not touched.

title: VS Code Insiders CachedData
why: Compiled code and extension downloads from VS Code Insiders. It makes new ones when it starts.

title: Windsurf caches
why: Compiled code, extension downloads and web caches from Windsurf. It rebuilds them when it starts.

title: Windsurf logs
why: Session logs from Windsurf. It writes new ones each time it starts.

title: Zed cache
why: Downloads and caches the Zed editor keeps. Zed fetches them again when needed.

title: Claude app caches
why: Web and graphics caches the Claude desktop app keeps. It rebuilds them; your chats are stored online.

title: Claude app cache
why: Downloads the Claude desktop app keeps. It fetches them again when needed.

title: Claude Code cache
why: Logs and temporary files from the Claude Code command-line tool. It makes new ones as it runs.

title: ChatGPT app cache
why: Images and web data the ChatGPT app keeps. It fetches them again; your chats are stored online.

title: Gemini app cache
why: Web data the Gemini app keeps. It fetches it again when needed.

title: GitHub Copilot cache
why: Downloads and caches GitHub Copilot keeps. It fetches them again when needed.

title: Ollama logs
why: Logs from Ollama. Your models are separate and stay put.

title: Ollama app cache
why: Caches the Ollama app keeps. Your models are separate and stay put.

title: Playwright browsers
why: Browsers Playwright downloaded for tests and AI agents. Reinstall with npx playwright install when needed.

title: uv cache
why: Python packages uv downloaded, kept to install faster. uv downloads them again when needed.

title: Hugging Face models
why: Models downloaded from Hugging Face. They can be very large to fetch again, so keep ones you use.

title: Hugging Face datasets
why: Datasets downloaded from Hugging Face. Keep ones you still train or test with.

title: Hugging Face download cache
why: Pieces of files kept so repeat Hugging Face downloads finish sooner. Downloads still work without them.

title: PyTorch hub cache
why: Models and weights PyTorch downloaded. Code that needs them downloads them again.

title: Whisper models
why: Speech models Whisper downloaded. It downloads them again the next time you transcribe.

title: Codex CLI logs
why: Logs from the Codex command-line tool. It writes new ones as it runs.

title: opencode cache
why: Packages and data the opencode tool downloaded. It fetches them again when needed.

title: Antigravity caches
why: Compiled code and web caches from the Antigravity editor. It rebuilds them when it starts.

title: LM Studio app caches
why: Web and graphics caches the LM Studio app keeps. Your models are separate and stay put.

title: Perplexity app cache
why: Web data the Perplexity app keeps. It fetches it again when needed.

title: Jupyter runtime files
why: Connection files left by Jupyter kernels that have stopped. Running kernels make new ones.
